candidate.name: write_policy_gate
candidate.hypothesis: The dominant failure mode of the identity baseline is silent policy-violating DB writes that the plain airline API accepts unchecked (cancel_reservation with none of the four policy grounds, send_certificate with no cancelled/delayed flight or ineligible compensation, route-changing update_reservation_flights). Refusing exactly those calls pre-execution with an actionable, DB-derived error will convert a meaningful share of DB-mismatch failures into passes with zero regression on the currently passing rollouts, because every passing rollout avoids those calls (0/22 passing rollouts invoked cancel_reservation or send_certificate).
candidate.changes: New plugin agents/write_policy_gate.py. register() rebinds tau2.domains.airline.tools.AirlineTools.use_tool in place (marker-guarded against double-patching) so that, before delegating to the original dispatch, it validates the current call against DB-provable policy preconditions and raises ValueError (surfaced to the model as an error tool message) only when a precondition is clearly violated. Three checks: (1) cancel_reservation blocked when the reservation is already cancelled, when any segment has departed/been flown (status flying/landed or a past date), or when none of business cabin / travel insurance / booked-within-24h / airline-cancelled flight holds; (2) send_certificate blocked unless the amount equals $100 x passengers for a reservation with an airline-cancelled segment, or $50 x passengers for a delayed one, and blocked for a regular member whose matching reservation has no insurance and is not business; (3) update_reservation_flights blocked when the proposed itinerary's first origin or last destination no longer matches the reservation's origin/destination/trip type. Each block message states the policy rule, the observed DB facts, and the compliant next step (deny/transfer). All checks are stateless, read only self.db and current kwargs, and defer to the original tool whenever data is missing. AgentHarness keeps the identity transform_request/transform_response API.
candidate.expected_efficiency: No prompt or schema changes, so token overhead is one lightweight validation pass per write call (negligible). Blocked-and-retried loops (e.g. repeated identical writes) should disappear, reducing turns and completion tokens on gated rollouts; unaffected rollouts see no measurable change.

candidate.name: bag_fee_normalizer
candidate.hypothesis: Every intended baggage-setting call satisfies nonfree_baggages = max(0, total_baggages - per-passenger free allowance(membership, cabin) * n_passengers); the plain API stores the field verbatim and charges 50*max(0, new_nonfree - old_nonfree), so the solver's allowance-ignoring splits produce DB states and payment histories that no intended outcome contains (observed in 6 rollouts across both evidence batches, in both directions, while all 8 distinct intended baggage actions lie on the invariant line). Repairing only the nonfree_baggages field at execution time will flip at least the currently failing DB check whose sole divergence is this field (the incumbent's task-33 trial-0 baggage write {2,1} vs intended {2,0}), with zero change on rollouts whose baggage writes are already allowance-consistent, because the repair fires only when the reservation's pre-state is itself on the invariant line and defers otherwise.
candidate.changes: New self-contained plugin agents/bag_fee_normalizer.py = agents/write_policy_gate.py copied verbatim (all three existing pre-execution blocks kept byte-identical: cancel_reservation preconditions, send_certificate amount/eligibility, update_reservation_flights route changes) plus exactly one new mechanism. A module constant _FREE holds the public checked-bag allowance table (regular 0/1/2, silver 1/2/3, gold 2/3/4 for basic_economy/economy/business), and _normalize_baggages(tools, tool_name, kwargs), called once from _gate before delegation, repairs kwargs['nonfree_baggages'] = max(0, total_baggages - per * n_passengers) when the call is update_reservation_baggages (reservation and booking-user resolved from tools.db.reservations/users, n = len(res.passengers), repair only if the current state satisfies nonfree == max(0, total - per*n)) or book_reservation (booking-user membership, kwargs cabin/passengers, no pre-state guard). The mechanism never raises and fails open (kwargs untouched) on missing reservation/user, unknown membership or cabin, malformed passenger lists, or non-int values; it does not touch total_baggages, payments, or any other tool, and adds no new error-message path. register() rebinds only tau2.domains.airline.tools.AirlineTools.use_tool behind a fresh idempotence marker and keeps AgentHarness as the identity transform_request/transform_response API. No new imports, no state, no runtime model/network/subprocess/filesystem calls.
candidate.expected_efficiency: No prompt or tool-schema changes and no added tool calls, so turns and completion tokens are unchanged; one O(1) table lookup plus arithmetic per booking/baggage call (negligible). Repaired calls remove a spurious $50 payment append, so affected rollouts end with a strictly smaller DB diff. Expected train mean 0.5333 -> ~0.55 from a deterministic replay flip of the repairable DB-only failure, with no regression surface on already-passing rollouts.

candidate.name: basic_economy_itinerary_gate
candidate.hypothesis: The solver's public system prompt states 'Basic economy flights cannot be modified' and 'all reservations, including basic economy, can change cabin without changing the flights', but the plain update_reservation_flights API enforces neither, so itinerary-changing calls on basic-economy reservations are silently accepted and produce DB states no intended outcome contains. Blocking update_reservation_flights (with an actionable policy error) exactly when the reservation's current cabin is basic_economy AND the proposed ordered (flight_number, date) sequence differs from the current one will flip at least the currently failing DB check in the incumbent's task-36 trial-0 rollout (accepted date shifts 2024-05-16 -> 2024-05-18 on basic_economy reservation EUJUY6; trial 1 passed with no writes and DB+COMMUNICATE basis, COMMUNICATE already 1.0 in trial 0) and up to three failing rollouts (task 36 trial 0; task 14 trial 0 and task 23 trial 1 via the explicit cancel-and-rebook redirect), with zero regression because all golden basic-economy updates preserve the itinerary exactly and 0 of the 37 passing rollouts issue any basic-economy itinerary-changing call (all 14 such calls across evidence batches sit in reward-0 rollouts).
candidate.changes: New self-contained plugin agents/basic_economy_itinerary_gate.py = agents/bag_fee_normalizer.py copied verbatim (all existing mechanisms kept byte-identical: cancel_reservation preconditions, send_certificate amount/eligibility, update_reservation_flights route check, and nonfree_baggages normalization) plus exactly one new mechanism. Module-level helper _seq(flights) returns the ordered list of (flight_number, date) pairs when flights is a non-empty list of dicts/objects with string fields, else None; _basic_economy_itinerary_gate(tools, res, flights) returns immediately unless res.cabin == 'basic_economy', returns when either sequence is None or cur == new (cabin-only changes on identical flights stay allowed, exactly as the public policy permits), and otherwise raises ValueError with a policy block message naming the rule, quoting both policy sentences, printing the observed current itinerary and the proposed one, and stating the compliant next steps (deny the modification, offer only policy-compliant options such as cancel-and-rebook or cabin-only change, transfer to a human agent if needed). _gate calls it as the first update_reservation_flights check, before the unchanged route check _update_gate. register() keeps the existing rebind of tau2.domains.airline.tools.AirlineTools.use_tool and rebinds only that, adds the _basic_economy_itinerary_gate marker, and guards idempotence on that marker. AgentHarness keeps the identity transform_request/transform_response API. No new imports, no state, no task IDs, no hardcoded reservation/flight identifiers, fail-open on every missing or malformed datum, no runtime model/network/subprocess/filesystem calls.
candidate.expected_efficiency: No prompt or tool-schema changes and no added tool calls, so turns, input and completion tokens are unchanged beyond the incumbent's observed band (5.73M-6.05M total). The gate ignores read calls and non-update writes, and for update_reservation_flights it exits on a cabin comparison or one O(n) itinerary comparison per call (n = segments), so overhead is negligible. Blocked calls replace calls that previously either wrote a spurious DB state (task 36 trial 0) or errored on payment grounds (tasks 14, 23), so no extra retry loops are introduced. Expected train mean 0.617 -> 0.633 (deterministic +1) with upside to 0.667 if the cancel-and-rebook redirect is followed on tasks 14/23; no regression surface on already-passing rollouts.

candidate.name: itinerary_continuity_gate
candidate.hypothesis: The plain airline API resolves itinerary writes by flight_number only: it never validates that the proposed flights form a connected chain or that the declared booking endpoints match the flights' actual route, so fabricated itineraries are stored verbatim. Across the 300 recorded rollouts there are exactly 12 reward-0 rollouts containing an accepted such call and 0 of the 163 passing rollouts contain one (passing rollouts: 157 have no violating call at all, 1 has none either, and 6 failing rollouts contain only already-errored violations). Rejecting exactly those calls pre-execution, with the resolved chain and an actionable next step, will flip the incumbent run's rollout whose only accepted write is such a call (batch_01 task-10 trial 0, where the task's golden state is the unchanged DB and COMMUNICATE is already 1.0: blocking the chain-broken update leaves the DB at the initial state), because the incumbent route check compares only first origin and last destination and lets an interior disconnection through.
candidate.changes: New self-contained plugin agents/itinerary_continuity_gate.py = agents/bag_fee_normalizer.py copied verbatim (AST-verified byte-identical for every pre-existing top-level def/class: cancel_reservation preconditions, send_certificate amount/eligibility, update_reservation_flights route check, nonfree_baggages allowance repair) plus exactly one new mechanism. Module-level `_chain(tools, flights)` resolves each flight entry to ordered (flight_number, origin, destination) from tools.db.flights and returns None as soon as any entry is not a dict/object with a readable flight_number or the flight is unknown, so the mechanism fails open on every missing or malformed datum. `_continuity_gate(tools, tool_name, kwargs)` returns immediately for any tool other than update_reservation_flights and book_reservation and for empty/non-list flights, then raises ValueError before any DB mutation when (a) any consecutive pair breaks connectivity (segment i destination != segment i+1 origin), (b) book_reservation with flight_type one_way has a first flight that does not depart kwargs['origin'] or a last flight that does not arrive kwargs['destination'], or (c) book_reservation with flight_type round_trip does not depart from and return to kwargs['origin']. Dates, segment counts, and all other conditions are deliberately not checked. Every message follows the file's existing 'POLICY BLOCK (<tool> <id>): <rule> Observed: <resolved chain> Do not ... <compliant next step>' style and is raised before execution so the environment returns it as an error tool message. register() keeps the existing rebind of tau2.domains.airline.tools.AirlineTools.use_tool, calls _continuity_gate immediately after the existing _gate call and before delegating to the original tool, sets a fresh _itinerary_continuity_gate marker, and extends the idempotence guard with that marker (all other register lines byte-identical). AgentHarness keeps the identity transform_request/transform_response API. No new imports (only tau2.domains.airline.tools.AirlineTools), no state, no task IDs, no hardcoded reservation/flight/user identifiers, no runtime model/network/subprocess/filesystem calls, and the new code never mutates kwargs or the DB.
candidate.expected_efficiency: No prompt or tool-schema changes and no added tool calls, so turns, input and completion tokens stay in the incumbent's band; the gate exits on a tool-name comparison for reads and non-itinerary writes and does one O(n) DB-truth resolution per itinerary call (n = segments), so overhead is negligible. Blocked calls replace calls that previously wrote a provably wrong DB state, and self-correcting retries consume at most one extra assistant step and ~100 tokens in the 2-3 of 60 rollouts touched per run. Expected incumbent val 0.55 -> 0.567 deterministic (the task-10 trial-0 DB returns to the golden unchanged state) with +0.02 to +0.05 upside as the other 10 touched failing rollouts across runs (tasks 15, 20, 23, 33, 34, 36) are forced into an actionable retry instead of storing a fabricated itinerary; regression surface measured over all five recorded runs is 0 of 163 passing rollouts, since no passing rollout contains such a call.

candidate.name: reservation_money_ledger
candidate.hypothesis: The plain airline API returns completed reservation writes only as a raw JSON dump of payment_history, and its book_reservation mismatch error states only 'total price is T, but paid P', so the exact money arithmetic never appears in a legible form: in the incumbent's 60-rollout run, 11 of 26 failures carry a payment-amount error, one rollout looped nine identical book_reservation calls on the unactionable mismatch message and ended by transferring, and one rollout executed the correct DB update (db_match true) yet told the user an incorrect refund figure while the required amount sat unread inside the returned payment_history. If every successful money-writing tool result appends a compact ledger line (per-entry payment id, signed amount with negative entries labelled as refunds, and the net) and the book_reservation mismatch error restates the required total, the paid sum, the signed difference, and the documented pricing composition, then the two rollouts whose only defect is money arithmetic or money communication flip to passes, lifting the incumbent from 0.5667 to at least 0.60, because both touchpoints change only the text of an already-returned or already-raised result and never alter which DB mutations execute; falsified if the incumbent stays at <= 0.5833, if either target rollout still fails, or if any currently passing rollout regresses on a money-writing task.
candidate.changes: New self-contained plugin agents/reservation_money_ledger.py = agents/itinerary_continuity_gate.py copied verbatim (AST-verified byte-identical for every pre-existing top-level def/class: cancel_reservation preconditions, send_certificate amount/eligibility, update_reservation_flights route check, nonfree_baggages allowance repair, itinerary continuity gate; only register() changed) plus exactly one new post-execution mechanism with two touchpoints on the same ledger computation. (1) Success path: a new outer wrapper around AirlineTools.use_tool, only for book_reservation, cancel_reservation, update_reservation_flights and update_reservation_baggages, duck-types the returned result's payment_history (list of entries with readable payment_id string and integer amount), and returns the serialized result plus one compact factual ASCII line 'Money ledger (reservation ID): charge <id> +<amt>; refund <id> -<amt>; net +<net>.' where serialization mirrors the plain environment's semantics (strings pass through, model_dump objects are json.dumps'ed with default=str); reads are never annotated, strings are never annotated, and any missing, malformed, or throwing datum returns the original result object unchanged (fail-open). (2) Error path: when the wrapped call raises a ValueError whose message contains the plain prefix 'Payment amount does not add up, total price is ' and the tool is book_reservation, the two integers are parsed from that message (never recomputed from the DB) and a ValueError is re-raised with the original message verbatim as prefix plus exactly one actionable sentence naming the required total, the paid sum, the signed difference, the declared passenger count/insurance/non-free baggage count from kwargs, and the documented pricing composition (flight prices, +$30 per passenger when insurance='yes', +$50 per non-free baggage); every other ValueError, including the existing POLICY BLOCK gate errors, propagates unchanged, and any parse failure re-raises the original error unchanged. register() keeps the incumbent's three layers and markers byte-identical (now behind an inverted guard so the new marker check is always reachable) and adds the outer layer behind its own _reservation_money_ledger marker, so repeated registration leaves exactly one wrapper per layer (verified). No task IDs, no reservation/flight/user identifiers, no expected answers, no cross-episode state, no filesystem/network/subprocess/model calls, no mutation of kwargs/results/DB; only json and re are added to the incumbent's tau2 import; AgentHarness keeps the identity transform_request/transform_response API. Mechanism distinct from all four prior rounds: none of the four pre-execution blocks or repairs is touched, and this candidate never blocks a call.
candidate.expected_efficiency: No prompt or tool-schema changes and no added tool calls; the ledger adds one short line (~25-40 tokens) to successful money-writing results (a few per rollout) and the enrichment replaces an already-raised error message with a slightly longer one, so input/completion token totals stay in the incumbent's band. The one rollout stuck retrying an unactionable mismatch nine times should exit the loop several turns earlier, so net turns and tokens are expected flat to slightly lower. Expected train mean 0.5667 -> ~0.60 (deterministic +2 of 60 rollouts: the looped-booking failure and the correct-DB-but-miscommunicated-refund failure), with upside if other mismatch-error rollouts (7 of 26 failures show the same plain prefix yet executed other wrong writes) self-correct faster from the arithmetic restatement; regression surface is limited to text formatting of write results, since no DB action, gate, or kwargs repair changes.
